questions: Did oval progress return to 0.95 or more with the restored kd? If not, which controller value moved it?
Did s-bend steering_oscillation stay at or below 0.3?
Did bend max_error stay on its 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau, and did excursions start before or after a line-loss event?

intent: Deliver the proven iteration 7 and 9 geometry unchanged (50 mm span at 12.5 mm pitch, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05, wheel_track 0.10, body 0.14 by 0.12 m, mass 0.7 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m). This keeps the best known platform for the final unseen-track race. The Integrator should hold the controller to the iteration 9 level (kd about 0.375, stable s-bend oscillation at or below 0.3) so that oval progress stays at or above 0.95.
learning: Iteration 10 showed that identical geometry with a different controller gives oval progress 0.727 and score 239.3, against 0.995 and 399.7 for the same geometry with the iteration 7 controller. The geometry is therefore not the only driver of score, and controller stability matters as much as sensing layout. Bend max_error has not responded to span, footprint, lead, wheel_track or controller changes, so the remaining unexplored lever (lead y 0.04, or a 16 mm footprint at 50 mm) is untested and was not used for the final design.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design I deliver is the one the unseen-track race will score. The best evidence is iteration 7 and iteration 9, which are the same geometry (50 mm span, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05, wheel_track 0.10). They scored 399.7 with oval progress 0.995 and 20 of 20 oval finishes. Iteration 10 reproduced this geometry with a retuned controller and fell to 239.3, with oval progress 0.727 and 6 of 20 finishes. That drop comes from the controller, not the geometry, because the geometry is identical. The Integrator is restoring kd to 0.375, so the geometry should stay as it is. The 60 mm span was rejected twice (iterations 3 and 8, oval progress 0.275 and 0.301). Bend max_error has stayed on its 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau across every span, footprint, lead, wheel_track and controller change, so no geometry lever has moved it below the off-track limit. The y 0.04 lead test is the next candidate lever, but it has not been verified and this is the last race. Testing it now risks a collapse like the y 0.03 result in iteration 1 and would give no later iteration to recover. I therefore hold the proven geometry and make no change. The expected result is the iteration 7 and 9 outcome, a score near 400 on the oval, with the bend tracks still off-track. Only the controller can change that outcome.
